provenance.title: 70°C PVC (Twin & Earth)
notes: Public reference checked: https://www.elandcables.com/media/3hoka0mu/table-4d5.pdf
Phase-specific columns; no interpolation. Large-conductor voltage drop uses tabulated impedance magnitude as a conservative bound.
Air 30C; D1 ground 20C, standard burial conditions. Balanced three-phase; harmonic neutral loading not assessed. Singles C uses touching/trefoil. Non-flexible copper only.
SWA minimum 1.5mm2. Armour fault withstand is not inferred. XLPE defaults to run at 70C; 90C needs equipment manufacturer confirmation.

70C SWA ratings and temperature guidance: https://electrical.theiet.org/wiring-matters/years/2022/93-november-2022/thermoplastic-pvc-or-thermosetting-xlpe-swa-cable/; voltage drop: https://www.elandcables.com/media/of4pe0xx/table-4d4a-and-4d4b.pdf

provenance.title: Installation and reference methods
notes: Letters A-G are reference-method codes, not Table 4A2 installation numbers.
Flat-cable choices 100-103 follow Table 4D5. 100: ceiling insulation <=100mm; 101: >100mm; 102: wall contact; 103: no wall contact. D is explicitly D1 (duct), not direct burial.
Construction filters only exclude incompatible choices; they do not verify a rating-table column.

provenance.title: Protective-device design Zs limits
notes: BS 7671:2018+A3:2024 is claimed by the existing code, not verified from a supplied source. Exact table, notes and disconnection applicability remain unverified.
An RCD alone provides no overload or short-circuit protection. RCBO overcurrent and residual-current functions require separate data.
MCCB/ACB settings, breaking capacity, energy let-through, selectivity and backup protection require manufacturer documentation; no generic values are supplied.
Isolation/switching suitability and residual-current protection have not been assessed.

provenance.title: Ambient-temperature correction factors
notes: Existing factors are for the legacy 70-degree thermoplastic-in-air assumption only; no 90-degree, buried-ground or mineral-insulated factors have been supplied.

provenance.title: Grouping correction factors
notes: Existing grouping factors have no verified arrangement/table/footnotes. They cannot establish applicability to other arrangements.

provenance.title: Copper conductor resistance
notes: Existing copper resistance rows are shared across tools. Conductor class, construction, source table and edition are unknown.
Resistance-only voltage-drop estimates omit reactance and do not establish current capacity, fault protection or minimum permitted conductor size.

provenance.title: Aluminium conductor resistance
notes: Only existing non-extrapolated rows are retained; conductor class, source table and edition are unknown.
A resistance row does not establish that the size is permitted for an installation.

provenance.title: Protective-conductor sizing assumptions
notes: Legacy separate-copper CPC sizing and flat-cable conductor pairings require verification against Tables 54.1-54.8.
R1+R2 is the sum of the two recorded conductor resistances; armour and missing CPC pairings are not substituted.

provenance.title: Design temperature and field-test comparisons
notes: The legacy design estimate multiplies circuit conductor resistance only by 1.2; external Ze is not multiplied. This is a declared approximation, not a verified correction for every cable temperature.
The 0.8 field-test comparison is separate from the design Zs limit. It is not mathematically equivalent to multiplying resistance by 1.2 and does not replace a detailed calculation.
IET guidance: https://electrical.theiet.org/bs-7671-18th-edition-wiring-regulations/faqs/inspection-and-testing-faqs/

provenance.title: Manufacturer device data
notes: Breaking capacity must be entered from the actual device/manufacturer documentation. No default manufacturer rating is assigned.
Fault-current comparison alone does not establish device suitability, selectivity, backup protection, energy let-through, residual protection or isolation.

provenance.title: Voltage-drop targets
notes: Legacy AC targets are 3 percent for lighting and 5 percent for other circuits. Appendix 4 applicability, supply origin and exceptions have not been source-verified.
DC targets are user-selected design targets; AC guidance is not silently applied as a DC regulatory limit.
